findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a named deliverable in the 'What' section describing the `enrich_operator_attested` changes (unconditional `incomplete_enumeration`→`none` on attestation; floor grades survive unchanged) so the function is not an AC-only orphan.
evidence: The four named structural changes in 'What' all target `impact_plan`; `enrich_operator_attested` is never mentioned in the 'What' body.

The AC introduces non-trivial behavioral rules: `incomplete_enumeration` → `none` unconditionally on attestation; floor grades survive unchanged. This is a distinct code path from `impact_plan`, not derivable from the four listed structural changes.
The AC itself says 'mirroring the `broken_oracle` rule' — this is a cross-cutting behavioral constraint the implementer must discover only by reading the ACs.
findings.finding: `enrich_operator_attested` behavioral rules for the new grades are specified only in an AC, with no corresponding description in the 'What' section. An implementer reading only the 'What' body would not know to touch this function at all.
findings.location: AC: '`enrich_operator_attested` handling is explicit and UNCONDITIONAL for the new grades'
scenarios: Implementer completes all four structural changes to `impact_plan`, ships plan-v4, and does not update `enrich_operator_attested`. Operator-attested findings with `contradicts_reality` or `omits_required_site` may be silently downgraded if the old attestation handler resets the axis to a prior default.
findings.suggested_fix: Under 'What' structural change item 5 (or a new sub-item), add: 'Update `enrich_operator_attested` to handle the new grades: on a recorded operator attestation, set `incomplete_enumeration` → `"none"` unconditionally (mirroring the `broken_oracle` rule); do NOT alter `contradicts_reality` or `omits_required_site` — they survive enrichment unchanged.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit rollback/back-out procedure to the 'What' section (e.g., 'to revert plan-v4: redeploy plan-v3 impact-model code; plan-v4-tagged sidecars are silently ignored by the v3 reader per the versioning invariant') so the deployment satisfies T4's reversibility requirement.
evidence: The plan says 'permissive-rollout invariant, version-tagging discipline, and no-pooling-across-versions rules all stand' (inherited from ADR 0036) but does not translate these into a concrete back-out procedure for plan-v4.

No AC verifies a rollback capability (e.g., a flag to revert to plan-v3 scoring, a deploy procedure, or a corpus-replay check to confirm the change does not exceed the expected PASS→BLOCK rate before promotion).
The three-way split is described as the 'pressure-release valve', but that is a design choice to reduce misfire risk — it is not a rollback mechanism for after deployment.
T4 criterion: 'The remedy for a destructive/breaking change is an explicit ROLLBACK / back-out plan or expand-contract sequencing — acknowledgement alone is insufficient.'
findings.finding: The plan acknowledges that the grading change will flip 42 findings from PASS to BLOCK (4.3% of affected runs) and explicitly cites the historical precedent of having to walk back a previous widening, yet provides no explicit rollback or back-out path for plan-v4 if the change over-fires in production.
findings.location: 'What' section — '42 of 983 runs flipping PASS→BLOCK, 4.3%... the LAST time this team widened a grade-blind hard floor it over-fired ~2x and had to be walked back'
scenarios: The `incomplete_enumeration` valve proves insufficient in the field; `omits_required_site` fires more broadly than the 42-finding corpus estimate; blocking rate spikes. Without a stated rollback path, the team must improvise a revert under pressure.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short 'Rollback' note in 'What': 'If plan-v4 over-fires in production: revert the `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` constant to `plan-v3` and redeploy. The version-tagging invariant (ADR 0036) guarantees plan-v4 sidecars are not read by the v3 scorer, so no data migration is needed. Gate the promotion with a corpus-replay assertion that the PASS→BLOCK flip rate stays within the expected 4.3% band.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an explicit, cheap rollback path for plan-v4 (e.g., a config-driven version-pin or feature flag that lets operators revert to plan-v3 scoring without a code deploy), and add an AC verifying it works.
evidence: 'the permissive-rollout invariant, version-tagging discipline, and no-pooling-across-versions rules all stand' — deferred to ADR 0036 without specifying the plan-v4-specific revert path

findings.finding: The plan asserts ADR 0036's permissive-rollout invariant 'stands' but does not specify the rollback procedure for plan-v4 itself: if the new omits_required_site/contradicts_reality grading causes over-blocking in production, there is no explicit, cheap, tested undo path described (e.g. a feature flag to fall back to plan-v3 scoring, or a version-pin mechanism that lets operators revert without a code deploy).
findings.location: What section — 'Two changes, landing together under ONE impact-model version bump' / AC: IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump
scenarios: Plan-v4 ships and omits_required_site fires on a class of findings that operators judge as false positives; with no flag or version-pin, the only recourse is a code revert + re-bump, which is slow and touches the calibration cohort boundary again.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm that ADR 0054 (or the IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION bump commit message) explicitly records WHY the policy document and the code change ship atomically — specifically that they share the plan-v4 version bump to avoid consuming two calibration-cohort closures — so the coupling rationale survives in the authoritative artifact, not only in this plan's prose.
evidence: 'Two changes, landing together under ONE impact-model version bump (plan-v4), because the bump closes the plan-v3 calibration cohort and we must not spend two.'
ADR 0054 is a docs-only artifact (status Accepted, no code change) that is independently mergeable and readable without the code change.

The version-bump coupling constraint is stated only in this plan's prose — a future reader arriving at ADR 0054 or the code diff will not see why they shipped together.
findings.finding: The plan bundles two independently-releasable outcomes — (1) the divergent_implementation grade-split code+schema+prompt change and (2) ADR 0054 (a pure policy document) — justified by a 'must not spend two version bumps' constraint that exists only in the plan's prose, not in ADR 0054's own stated rationale.
findings.location: ## What — opening paragraph ('Two changes, landing together under ONE impact-model version bump (plan-v4), because the bump closes the plan-v3 calibration cohort and we must not spend two.')
scenarios: A reviewer or future calibration author reads ADR 0054 in isolation and cannot understand why the policy and the code change are atomically coupled.

findings.suggested_fix: Add a 'Context / Coupling Rationale' section to ADR 0054 stating: 'This ADR ships in the same plan-v4 version bump as the divergent_implementation grade-split (see implementation plan) because both changes close the plan-v3 calibration cohort; issuing a second bump would split the cohort boundary and violate the no-pooling-across-versions invariant of ADR 0036.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` is warranted: if the only two uses remain co-located inside `impact_plan`, consider inlining the exclusion as `if a not in ("ac_unverifiable", "divergent_implementation")` (matching the existing inline `_ORACLE_FLOOR_GRADES` OR-check pattern) rather than introducing a named tuple with only 2 intra-function call-sites.
evidence: Current codebase: the `if a != "ac_unverifiable"` exclusion appears exactly twice in `decide.py` — line 361 (contribution loop) and line 373 (override loop) — both inside the ~20-line `impact_plan` function.
After the plan lands, both exclusions become `if a not in _PLAN_GRADED_AXES`; still 2 sites, 0 external callers.

`ORACLE_GRADE01` (the precedent being mirrored) does NOT require a parallel `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES`-style indirection: the oracle exclusion is expressed as a direct `if a != "ac_unverifiable"` guard and has worked correctly since plan-v3.
Rule-of-Three: a shared constant is justified when ≥3 independent sites reference it; 2 co-located uses inside one function do not clear that bar.
findings.finding: `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES = ("ac_unverifiable", "divergent_implementation")` has only 2 projected call-sites, both within the single `impact_plan` function body, falling below the Rule-of-Three threshold for a named abstraction.
findings.location: What → Change 1 → named structural change #3: 'introduce `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` … and drive both the contribution loop and the override loop off it'
scenarios: A reader arriving at `impact_plan` must look up `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` to understand what the exclusion guard means, adding indirection where the existing inline `if a != 'ac_unverifiable'` pattern is already self-explanatory.
If a third kind-graded axis is added in the future, `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` becomes justified — but that is exactly the YAGNI/R-o-3 anti-pattern: abstracting for a future case that has not happened.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` constant with an inline guard `if a not in ("ac_unverifiable", "divergent_implementation")` in both the contribution loop and the override loop inside `impact_plan`. Add a comment: `# kind-graded axes — excluded from _SEV01 loop; each has its own GRADEXX map`. This preserves the co-location and the self-documenting comment without a premature abstraction. Promote to `_PLAN_GRADED_AXES` only if a third kind-graded axis is added.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Clarify and justify the `incomplete_enumeration → 'none'` operator-attestation clearing: explain why an operator-attested AC cures a cosmetic site-coverage omission (not just an AC verifiability concern), AND specify whether the trigger is (a) the existing per-finding text-match against attested AC oracle text, or (b) a broader 'any attestation present' condition — then verify the chosen trigger will actually fire for typical incomplete_enumeration findings.
evidence: incomplete_enumeration grades 'a site is omitted but touching it is optional/cosmetic (docs, comments, a redundant mention)' — a code-site coverage concern, not an AC verifiability concern
operator attestation cures AC verifiability (mirrors broken_oracle rule, which gates on `ac_unverifiable in ('missing_oracle', 'underspecified_oracle')`), not code site coverage

existing enrich_operator_attested trigger: fires only when a finding's combined text (location + finding + checklist_item + evidence) contains the attested AC's oracle text (workflow_ops.py:119); an incomplete_enumeration finding about a missing file mention is unlikely to reference AC oracle text
plan analogizes to 'mirroring the `broken_oracle` rule' without explaining why the semantics transfer from AC-oracle-verifiability to code-site-coverage

findings.finding: The `enrich_operator_attested` clearing of `incomplete_enumeration → 'none'` on an operator attestation lacks a coherent semantic justification, and the existing trigger mechanism (finding text contains an attested AC's oracle text) will silently miss most `incomplete_enumeration` findings in practice.
findings.location: AC: '`enrich_operator_attested` handling is explicit and UNCONDITIONAL for the new grades: on a recorded operator attestation it MUST set `incomplete_enumeration` to `none`'
scenarios: A G7 finding grades divergent_implementation=incomplete_enumeration for an omitted doc comment — the finding body references no operator-attested AC text, so the enrich trigger never fires and the 'unconditional' clearing never happens

If the intent is 'clear for ALL incomplete_enumeration findings when any attestation exists,' the plan requires a structural change to enrich_operator_attested that is broader than the existing per-finding text-match pattern — and the plan does not specify this

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a plan section (or expand the versioning AC) specifying the exact mechanism by which plan-v3/v2 corpus records with `divergent_implementation: "high"|"medium"|"low"` are deserialized without error under plan-v4 code (e.g., a version-discriminated union model, a read-time coercion shim, or a separate v3 `TypeAdapter`), and confirm the test exercises at least one such legacy value rather than only new-format fixtures.
evidence: AC: 'legacy plan-v3/v2 sidecars still read without error. Verified: test_impact_model_versioning.py pins updated and green.'

The plan changes PlanSeverityAttrs.divergent_implementation to Literal["none","contradicts_reality","omits_required_site","incomplete_enumeration"] — making "low"/"medium"/"high" parse errors — but does not say how 51,964 existing corpus records carrying those old values are deserialized under plan-v4 code.
ABSENCE: no mention of a version-discriminated deserializer, union type, or coercion shim anywhere in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan changes `divergent_implementation` to a closed Literal that makes old ordinal values (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) parse errors, and asserts "legacy plan-v3/v2 sidecars still read without error" — but nowhere specifies the mechanism that achieves this (union type, version-gated model, read-time coercion, separate deserializer). Without specifying the mechanism, there is no way to verify that reading the existing 51,964-entry plan-v3 corpus under plan-v4 code is safe, batched, or idempotent. The AC only verifies the outcome via a test; it does not require the implementation to be documented.
findings.location: AC: `legacy plan-v3/v2 sidecars still read without error` / `test_impact_model_versioning.py` pin
scenarios: A replay of the plan-v3 corpus under plan-v4 code triggers Pydantic ValidationError on every record where divergent_implementation was 'high', 'medium', or 'low', breaking the calibration tooling the plan depends on.
The test uses a hand-crafted two-field sidecar fixture that avoids old ordinal values, giving a false green while production corpus replay still fails.
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a versioned deserialization path: when the sidecar's `IMPACT_MODEL_VERSION` tag is `plan-v3` or earlier, deserialize `divergent_implementation` via a `Literal["none","low","medium","high"]`-typed model and coerce `"low"`→`"incomplete_enumeration"`, `"medium"`/`"high"`→`"omits_required_site"` (or a sentinel `"_legacy_ordinal"` that scores as 0.0 for replay purposes). The versioning test should assert round-trip deserialization of a plan-v3 fixture that carries `divergent_implementation: "high"`.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a rollback-state assertion to the plan: specify what plan-v3 code does with plan-v4-tagged sidecar records (e.g., 'version-unknown records are skipped during corpus replay') and confirm no calibration data loss occurs on partial rollback — attach a `DATA LOSS RISK` note if plan-v4 corpus entries cannot be re-read by plan-v3 code.
evidence: 'landing together under ONE impact-model version bump (plan-v4), because the bump closes the plan-v3 calibration cohort'
ABSENCE: no rollback path description, no assertion that plan-v3 code gracefully ignores or errors on plan-v4-tagged corpus entries, no 'DATA LOSS RISK' note.
The plan's own ADR 0036 reference ('permissive-rollout invariant... all stand') implies rollback is a valid operational mode, but the corpus-state consequence is unspecified.
findings.finding: The plan does not assert the post-rollback schema state for plan-v4 corpus entries written between a plan-v4 deployment and a hypothetical rollback to plan-v3 code. Corpus entries written with new grade values (`"omits_required_site"`, `"contradicts_reality"`, `"incomplete_enumeration"`) are unreadable by plan-v3's `PlanSeverityAttrs` if it used the old ordinal Literal. The plan says the version bump 'closes the plan-v3 cohort' but does not say what plan-v3 code does with plan-v4-tagged records during a rollback window.
scenarios: A bug in plan-v4 forces a rollback to plan-v3 within days of deployment; plan-v3 impact_plan code encounters corpus records tagged plan-v4 with divergent_implementation='omits_required_site' and either crashes or silently scores them 0.0, corrupting the calibration signal.

Rollback exits 0 (plan-v3 code is running) but the corpus now contains an irrecoverable mix of v3 and v4 records that cannot be cleanly replayed under either version's model without the coercion layer.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add canonical worked examples (one per grade, matching the ac_unverifiable block's format) for `contradicts_reality` and `incomplete_enumeration` to the plan's AC or a co-located prompt-authoring note, so implementors have prescribed calibrating text for both grades when updating the verifier prompts.
evidence: Plan AC states: 'define all three grades with a worked example each, in the same shape as the ac_unverifiable oracle-kind block'

ac_unverifiable block in plan_review_verifier.md (lines 68-80) shows concrete, operational worked examples for each oracle kind (what makes a valid missing_oracle, broken_oracle, underspecified_oracle example)
Plan's triggering bug description provides a concrete `omits_required_site` scenario (four sites branching on `"s3vectors"` omitted from scope)
No worked-example content is provided in the plan for `contradicts_reality` (a named symbol/file/behavior that does not exist as described) or `incomplete_enumeration` (an optional/cosmetic omission)

The verification command only checks `grep -c "omits_required_site" ... >= 1 per file`, so a prompt update that adds only `omits_required_site` with an example satisfies the AC even if the other two grades are bare definitions
findings.finding: The plan mandates 'a worked example each' for all three new `divergent_implementation` grades in both verifier prompts but provides zero worked-example content for `contradicts_reality` and `incomplete_enumeration`. Only `omits_required_site` has illustrative source material (the triggering bug). An implementor must invent calibration examples for two of the three grades without guidance, risking inconsistent or mis-calibrated prompt wording — exactly the failure mode this plan is intended to fix.
findings.location: AC: 'Both verifier prompts define all three grades with a worked example each, in the same shape as the ac_unverifiable oracle-kind block.'
scenarios: A developer writes the prompt update, adds all three grade labels, provides a concrete example for `omits_required_site` (cribbed from the bug), but writes only one-line definitions for the other two — the AC grep passes, but the LLM verifier has no calibrating examples for `contradicts_reality` and `incomplete_enumeration`, perpetuating the mis-grading the plan is trying to fix.

Without a canonical example of `contradicts_reality`, two different implementors may write examples that calibrate differently (e.g. one uses a 'wrong file name in scope' example, another uses a 'non-existent API claimed'), leading to divergent LLM grading behavior across model versions.
findings.suggested_fix: In the AC (or a 'prompt-authoring guidance' subsection), add inline worked examples following the ac_unverifiable pattern, e.g.: `contradicts_reality` — 'The plan states the impact model reads divergent_implementation via DIVERGENCE_GRADE01, but no such map exists in decide.py — the named symbol does not exist as described.' `incomplete_enumeration` — 'The plan omits updating the CHANGELOG entry for the new grade, but CHANGELOG updates are cosmetic and the goal holds without them.'

findings.finding: The G7 criterion prompt (plan_review_G7.md) and its eval spec (plan-review-g7.eval.yaml) are unenumerated consumers of the divergent_implementation axis. findings.location: Plan section 'What / 1. Grade divergent_implementation by DIVERGENCE KIND' — unenumerated edit targets: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/plan_review_G7.md, src/rebar/llm/eval_specs/plan-review-g7.eval.yaml

findings.finding: AC 1's proving command `grep -c "corpus replay\|dogfood" docs/adr/0054-*.md` counts lines containing EITHER term and asserts `>= 2`, but this does NOT guarantee both terms appear. A file with 'corpus replay' on two separate lines and 'dogfood' absent would return 2, satisfying the check while violating the stated intent that both permitted A/B forms are documented.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — first bullet: `grep -c "corpus replay\|dogfood" docs/adr/0054-*.md` returns >= 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the single `grep -c "corpus replay\|dogfood" ...` with two commands: `grep -q 'corpus replay' docs/adr/0054-*.md && grep -q 'dogfood' docs/adr/0054-*.md` (exits 0 only when both terms appear).

findings.finding: AC10 (docs guide) asserts 'the guide is regenerated from the registry, not hand-edited' but provides no concrete proving command that an executor can run to verify this property.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — final AC (docs/plan-review-gate.md and generated docs/plan-review-criteria-guide.md)

findings.finding: AC 9's proving command uses `grep -rn` with BRE-style grouping `'\(high\|medium\|low\)'`, where `\|` alternation is a GNU extension not present in POSIX BRE. On non-GNU `grep` implementations (macOS default, BSD) this pattern silently fails to match anything, making the 'no matches' result meaningless — a missed fixture would not be detected.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — second-to-last bullet: `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/`
findings.suggested_fix: Replace `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/` with `grep -rEn '"divergent_implementation": "(high|medium|low)"' tests/ src/`.

findings.finding: Two AC verification shell commands use GNU grep BRE alternation (`\|`) that is unsupported on macOS BSD grep, causing the checks to silently produce wrong results on the macOS developer-workstation cell of the support matrix.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — fixture-migration AC: `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "\(high\|medium\|low\)"' tests/ src/`; ADR content AC: `grep -c "corpus replay\|dogfood" docs/adr/0054-*.md`
findings.suggested_fix: Use `grep -E` (POSIX extended regex, supported by both GNU and BSD grep): `grep -rn '"divergent_implementation": "(high|medium|low)"' tests/ src/` and `grep -cE 'corpus replay|dogfood' docs/adr/0054-*.md`.
